draft.title: Six Principles of Harmony for Children: A Dhamma Class at BMC
draft.body:
On September 13, 2026, children and families gathered at the Buddha Meditation Center of Greater Washington DC for a special children’s Dhamma class exploring the six principles of harmony for children. Inspired by the Kosambiya Sutta, the class introduced timeless Buddhist teachings in a way that could meet young learners in their daily lives.

Rather than approaching harmony as an abstract idea, the session invited children to consider how kindness, sharing, and mindful communication can guide the way they relate to one another. A caring word, a willingness to include someone, or a moment taken to listen can each become a small but meaningful practice at home, in the classroom, and among friends.

The class centered on a simple reminder: “Spread kindness even at difficult times.” Children encounter misunderstandings, disappointment, and conflict just as adults do. Learning to pause, respond gently, and remember the well-being of others can give them practical tools for meeting those moments with greater confidence and care.

The six principles of harmony for children offer a helpful foundation for emotional balance and connection. When Buddhist teachings are explored through familiar situations, children can see that the Dhamma is not only something to learn about; it is something to practice in the choices they make each day.

We are grateful to the children and families who shared this time of learning together. May the seeds of kindness, generosity, and mindful speech continue to grow in their homes, schools, and communities. May all beings be happy and peaceful. 🙏

pack.description:
Six Principles of Harmony for Children
In our children’s Dhamma class, young learners explored the six principles of harmony from the Kosambiya Sutta to cultivate kindness, sharing, and mindful communication.

On September 13, 2026, children and families gathered at the Buddha Meditation Center of Greater Washington DC for a special children’s Dhamma class centered on learning the six principles of harmony. In a world full of rapid interactions and social challenges, cultivating early habits of empathy and emotional balance gives young minds the tools they need to navigate relationships with confidence. Rather than presenting Buddhist teachings as abstract philosophy, the session focused on making foundational wisdom relatable, showing children how timeless principles can be practiced at home, in the classroom, and with their peers every day.
pack.quote: Spread kindness even at difficult times.
